extracted.intended_audience: small business applicants preparing NIH SBIR/STTR (PHS/NIH/NIAID) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH SBIR/STTR (Phase I R41/R42) application including SF424/R&R and PHS398 research plan materials for a preclinical therapeutic project (peptide therapeutic for T1D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity's instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FOA-specific instructions (page limits, forms, required attachments). Do not assume a sample application matches current FOA formatting or requirements; check the current FOA and agency sample repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract required
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Summary/Abstract that concisely describes the problem, significance, translational rationale, preliminary data, and the goals of the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should summarize disease context, mechanism, preliminary efficacy, and proposed goals (e.g., establish clinical parameters, impact on glucose tolerance, insulin and c-peptide measurements). Attach as the Project Summary/Abstract file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative required
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Project Narrative that succinctly communicates public health relevance and the high-level approach (e.g., rationale for CD40–CD154 peptide approach to control autoimmune inflammation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Project Narrative to state the potential public health impact and translational intent of the work; it complements the abstract and specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims and Research Strategy sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Specific Aims and a Research Strategy describing goals, experiments, expected outcomes, milestones, timeline, and future plans (Phase 2 activities such as PK/toxicology and IND-readiness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe aims clearly (Goal #1, #2, #3 etc.), experimental design, time frames (e.g., 12 months for Phase I activities), contingencies, and how success will be evaluated (outcomes and concerns, alternative plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe available facilities, lab space, contractual arrangements, core facilities, equipment access, and institutional approvals (IRB, IACUC) that support project execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics (square footage, dedicated wet bench space, HPLC, flow cytometers, microscopy cores, mass spectrometers) and note formal agreements or access arrangements with institutions or centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment listing
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment available for the project (e.g., flow cytometers, centrifuges, FPLC, mass spectrometers, Agilent HPLC, microplate readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include equipment relevant to proposed assays and analyses to demonstrate capability to perform the work without major equipment purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch (Biosketch) format and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Biographical Sketches for senior/key personnel following NIH format; 'DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.' Include education/training, personal statement, positions/honors, contributions to science, and research support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NIH biosketch structure and page limits exactly; include a personal statement linking expertise to project and list active/current & pending support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed profile data for each senior/key person including role, degree, percent effort, and attached biographical sketch and current & pending support files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify project roles (e.g., PD/PI, medical advisor), contact info, and upload required attachments in the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects involvement declaration and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether human subjects are involved. If yes, indicate exemption status or IRB approval dates and provide Human Subject Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, include protections, consent procedures, and assurance numbers; if no, mark 'No' explicitly. Attach IRB documentation when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals section and IACUC documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For vertebrate animal use, indicate whether animals are used, whether IACUC review is pending/approved, provide IACUC approval date and Animal Welfare Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include species/strains, justification for use, procedures, and welfare oversight details. Provide IACUC protocol numbers or pending status as required by the FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of animal numbers and statistical powering
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify the number of animals with statistical sample size calculations (alpha levels, power/confidence) and the basis for effect-size estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide power calculations and cite the tool/method used (e.g., GraphPad Prism, ClinCal.com). Explain group sizes, treatment groups, and how numbers were derived to achieve statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterinary care and animal welfare procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe veterinary care, housing facility accreditation, measures to alleviate discomfort/distress, use of analgesics when appropriate, and criteria for euthanasia or intervention (e.g., insulin administration for diabetic mice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference institutional accreditation (PHS, AAALAC), availability of veterinarians, monitoring frequency, and humane endpoints. Explain how procedures minimize pain or distress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia method specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify euthanasia methods consistent with accepted guidelines (example: controlled CO2 exposure followed by cervical dislocation) and note that methods are approved by institutional and authoritative panels (e.g., AVMA, local IACUC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the euthanasia protocol explicitly and cite approval by the institutional IACUC and recognized authority panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer whether the project has potential impact on the environment and, if so, indicate whether an exemption, Environmental Assessment (EA), or Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) has been performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If environmental impacts exist, provide explanations and documentation of any required NEPA reviews or exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether select agents will be used in the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no select agents, explicitly state 'No'. If yes, provide appropriate registration, biosafety, and compliance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed budget (Total Federal Funds Requested, Total Non-Federal Funds, Program Income) and attach a Budget Justification supporting requested costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Research & Related Budget forms for each year and any consortium/subaward budgets. Justify personnel, supplies, animals, and subaward costs in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan(s) and intellectual property disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe resource sharing plans and explicitly state proprietary materials or patent coverage; identify limitations on sharing (e.g., proprietary peptides with patent coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare patents/PCT/office actions and state how proprietary items will be handled. If resources are proprietary, explain sharing restrictions and commercialization intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverables, milestones, and go/no-go criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Define measurable deliverables, milestones, timelines, and criteria for lead candidate selection or progression to Phase II (e.g., dose response, routes of administration, PK/tox studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific milestones (e.g., determine GTT improvement, insulin/c-peptide maintenance, dose/route optimization) and contingency plans if milestones are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design and outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe in detail experimental procedures, routes of administration, dosing regimens, outcome measures (e.g., glucose tolerance testing, serum insulin and c‑peptide assays, histology/islet mass, islet infiltration), and endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define time points (weekly GTT up to 12 weeks), number of animals per group, controls (scrambled peptides, vehicle), and specific assays to be used to assess efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan and concerns/limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the statistical analysis approach, how data will be compared over time, and a discussion of expected outcomes and potential technical issues or limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify statistical tests, confidence/alpha levels, planned comparisons, and how lack of observed differences will be handled (e.g., alter dosing strategy and re-examine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II planning: PK, toxicology, and regulatory preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: State Phase II activities and timelines including pharmacokinetics (PK), toxicology studies, drug formulation scaling, and IND filing preparations (engage experts/consultants and CROs as needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify collaborators/consultants (e.g., peptide drug development experts, IND consultants like CliniPace), and describe patent/IP status and plans for commercialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: References Cited and supporting literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a Bibliography & References Cited section documenting prior publications, preliminary data sources, and relevant literature that support the rationale and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite key prior work demonstrating mechanism, preliminary efficacy, and translational relevance (e.g., prior Diabetologia 2014 peptide study, mechanistic J Immunol papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and institutional compliance statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include required administrative certifications and assurances (signatures certifying the statements are true and compliance with federal regulations), authorized representative signatures, and executive order review status (E.O. 12372).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and sign SF424 certifications and indicate whether the application is subject to State review under E.O. 12372.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and confidentiality awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that NIH responses to FOIA requests may result in substantial redactions to protect confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments/deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that awardee-provided materials posted by NIH for educational purposes may be subject to FOIA and will be redacted accordingly; plan how proprietary information is described and submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of required attachments and registration details
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach all required files (Project Summary, Project Narrative, Facilities, Equipment, Bibliography, Biographical Sketches, Current & Pending Support, SBC registration/control ID) and provide organizational identifiers (DUNS, EIN/TIN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SBC registration (SBC Control ID), organizational DUNS, and tax identifiers are current and included with the SF424 package to avoid administrative errors or delays.
